title: How do I get to the cathedral?
goal: Get around town: ask for directions, use place prepositions without changing the noun, and see why Bulgarian uses one word, **къде**, for both "where" and "where to".
bekal: ask for directions and understand the answer
use the command form to give directions

dialogs.title: Диалог — Lost in the city center
dialogs.intro: Ani is looking for the Alexander Nevsky Cathedral, the gold-domed building that's Sofia's landmark. Notice that the place names never change form, however often the preposition changes.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: Excuse me, how do I get to the cathedral?
lines.literal: excuse-(formal), how — that — reach-I — to — cathedral-the?

lines.speaker: Жена:
lines.id: Are you on foot or by car?

lines.speaker: Жена:
lines.id: No, ten minutes. Go straight along this street.
lines.literal: no, ten — minutes. walk-(formal) — straight — along — this — street.

lines.speaker: Жена:
lines.id: Yes. At the second intersection turn right.
lines.literal: yes. at — second-the — intersection — turn-(formal) — to-the-right.

lines.speaker: Жена:
lines.id: Then you'll see a big park. The cathedral is behind the park.
lines.literal: then — will — see-you — big — park. cathedral-the — is — behind — park-the.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: I can't miss it, can I?
lines.literal: not — can — that — it-(f) — miss-I, isn't-it?

lines.speaker: Жена:
lines.id: No way! The domes are gold.

notes: **Как да стигна до…? is the key sentence of this unit.** Literally "how that I reach to…", it uses the *да* pattern from Unit 8. Learn it whole; it will save you in any city.

**Means of transport take с — "with".** *С колата* (by car), *с автобус* (by bus), *с влак* (by train), *с метрото* (by metro). For walking there's a separate word: **пеша**. ⚠️ Don't say *с крака*; it sounds like carrying your feet along as luggage.

**По тази улица means "along this street".** The preposition **по** is used for movement *along* something: *по улицата* (along the street), *по стълбите* (up/down the stairs). Compare *на улицата* — being in the street, without movement.

**Вървете and завийте are formal commands.** To one person you know well, the forms are *върви* and *завий*. Formal commands almost always end in **-те**, and you'll hear them from everyone who gives you directions.

**Ordinal numbers follow gender and carry the article.** *На втората пресечка* — at the second intersection (*пресечка* is feminine). *На втория етаж* — on the second floor (*етаж* is masculine). Notice that the article sticks to **the number**, not to the noun.

**Не може да я пропусна — the short pronoun я stands for the cathedral.** *Катедрала* is feminine, so the pronoun is *я* ("her"), where English says "it". Note its position: between *да* and the verb, just like *се* in Unit 9.
**Няма начин literally means "there's no way"**, and it's used exactly like English *no way*, both for impossible things and for a firm refusal.

**The "Свети Александър Невски" Cathedral was built in memory of the two hundred thousand Russian soldiers who fell in the war that freed Bulgaria in 1877–78.** Its domes are covered in real gold, and the crypt holds one of the largest collections of Orthodox icons in Europe. If you go in: cover your shoulders, and don't take photos inside without permission.

grammars.title: Къде — one word for "where" and "where to"
body: Bulgarian doesn't distinguish between where you are and where you're going, either in the question word or in the form of the noun. Only the verb tells you the direction — just as in English.
after: Compare Russian, which demands *где* vs *куда*, *в Москве* vs *в Москву*. Bulgarian has thrown all of that away, and nothing is lost — the context is always enough. It's one of the reasons Bulgarian is much easier for beginners than its Slavic relatives.

grammars.title: The command form
body: Just two forms: one for someone you call *ти*, one for *вие*. The second is always the first plus **-те**.
after: To forbid something, just add **не** in front — but with the ongoing form of the verb: *Не закъснявай!* (don't be late), *Не влизайте!* (don't go in).
⚠️ **Ела and елате are very irregular** and look nothing like the dictionary form *дойда*. Learn them separately; you'll hear them every day.

sections.title: Asking for directions and understanding the answer

head: Asking
Say it
Meaning
rows: Може ли да ми покажете на картата?
MO-zheh lee da mee po-KA-zheh-teh na KAR-ta-ta
Could you show me on the map?

blocks.text: If the answer is too fast, one sentence will save you: **Може ли по-бавно, моля?** (Could you say it more slowly, please?). Bulgarians almost always repeat it patiently right away — and often walk part of the way with you.

Ordinal numbers behave like adjectives: they follow the gender of the noun, and when used with the article, the article sticks to them. *Първият автобус* (the first bus), *първата спирка* (the first stop), *първото дете* (the first child).

blocks.title: The Sofia metro and its archaeological surprises
items: Sofia has a clean, cheap, easy-to-read metro — three lines, with signs in both Cyrillic and Latin letters. What makes it special: while the tunnels were being dug, workers kept finding the ruins of the Roman city of **Serdica** under the center.

Instead of clearing them away, Sofia built the *Сердика* station around them. You step off the train and walk among eighteen-centuries-old Roman paving stones, under glass, in the middle of rush hour.
Even the city's name comes from the church of **Света София** — Holy Wisdom. If you want one sentence to compliment the city: *София е много стар град.* (Sofia is a very old city.)
How do I get to the station?
Go straight on and turn left. (formal)
The cathedral is behind the park.

Put the words in the right order.
Change the command from ти to вие.

answers: Как да стигна до гарата? — Къде е спирката? — Далече ли е? — Изгубих се. — Вървете направо и завийте наляво. — Катедралата е зад парка.
Как да стигна до катедралата? — Вървете направо по тази улица. — На втората пресечка завийте надясно. — Изгубих се. — Няма начин.
Вървете направо! — Завийте надясно! — Елате тук! — Седнете, моля! — Изчакайте малко!
